To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the domain wall in a ferromagnet with a pair of uniformly magnetized nanoparticles can be trapped in one of four different positions depending on the relative orientation of the magnetic moment of the nanoparticles with respect to the direction of magnetization of the ferromagnet, and the domain wall can be trapped in a stable state in the absence of external magnetic fields.

the domain wall pinning in the planar ferromagnet consisting of a nanomagnet with the magnetic domain wall and two nanoparticles is determined by the relative orientations of the magnetic moments of nanoparticles with respect to the magnetization of nanomagnet and the magnetic moment of nanomagnet.
domain walls in a nanowire can be pinned by the stray fields of nanoparticles and that this pinning is determined by the relative magnetic moment orientations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of domain walls and stray magnetic fields of magnetic nanoparticles.
the study of magnetic properties of ferromagnetic nano-objects.
the study of domain wall dynamics in ferromagnetic systems with the use of micromagnetic simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pinning of the domain wall by the magnetic field of a nanoparticle depends on the magnetic configuration of the system and is determined by the magnetic configuration of nanoparticles and nanowire.
the magnetic properties of the nanoparticles and their interaction with the nanowire determine the domain wall pinning in the nanowire.
, the domain wall pinning is a very effective method to control the magnetization of a nanowires.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stray field of a nanoparticle can pin domain walls in a ferromagnet, but the domain wall pinning effect can be significantly enhanced by the magnetic anisotropy of the ferromagnetic material.
domain wall pinning by stray fields of two uniformly magnetized particles is possible in a ferromagnet with a single magnetic domain wall, which is a new result.
the stray fields of magnetic particles can be used to manipulate the domain walls in a ferromagnet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stray fields of nanoparticles can be used to pin a domain wall in a ferromagnet.
domain wall pining in the nanowire by magnetic stray fields of the nanoparticles can be achieved by controlling the relative orientation of the magnetization of these two magnetic systems.
the domain wall pinning by the stray fields of the magnetic nanoparticles can be controlled by changing the relative orientation of their magnetic moment and the magnetization in the nanowire.
